move: ranked rows slide in, bars expand with counters, sheen sweeps, retract
how: A white leaderboard card with six rows built from data: rank, coloured initial avatar, name, a grey track with a coloured fill sized to the value, and a number. The card rises y:30 (power3.out) and the heading slides up. From 7% rows slide in from x:-80/opacity:0 with expo.out staggered 0.09; the grey tracks scale scaleX from 0 (left origin) 0.1s later, then each fill expands scaleX 0 to 1 over 1s with expo.out (stagger 0.09) starting at 15% while a per-row counter ticks to its value with the same ease. Hold at 50%: a CSS sheen (a translucent white gradient ::after positioned by a --sheen custom property) sweeps left to right across each bar via an object tween from -100% to 300% (power2.inOut, stagger 0.06). Exit at 79%: fills collapse scaleX to 0 with expo.in staggered from the last row, numbers fade, rows slide back out x:-60 from the bottom up, card fades.
adapt: Edit the data array of [name, initials, value, colour] (any row count) and the heading; the max value (128) normalises widths and must match the top row; keep the expo.out row-then-bar cascade and the sheen sweep in the hold.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and generates .row elements from shot.rows; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with rows at 0.07-0.4 of D, sheen at 0.5, collapse at 0.79. The sheen is driven by setting a CSS custom property in onUpdate, which ports directly; getElementById and querySelectorAll must be scoped to el.
caveats: sheen relies on a ::after pseudo-element reading a --sheen custom property
from() tweens on generated rows need the DOM built before the timeline
